dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: kramadvādaśakaṃ samyag dvādaśākṣarabheditam | sthūlasūkṣmaparasthityā muktvā muktvāntataḥ śivaḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: Twelve stations in sequence, each properly marked by one of twelve letters: attend to each in its gross, then subtle, then supreme form, leaving each behind in turn; in the end there is Śiva.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh's notes list the twelve stations (janmāgra at the level of the generative organ, mūla, kanda, nābhi, hṛd, kaṇṭha, tālu, bhrūmadhya, lalāṭa, brahmarandhra, śakti, vyāpinī) and pair them with twelve vowels (a ā i ī u ū e ai o au aṃ aḥ). The verse itself names neither the stations nor the letters: both lists are commentary.

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand. Verse number verified; the twelve stations and twelve vowels are verified only as Singh's commentary, not as verse text.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y4 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 30 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: twelve stations in rising sequence (locations given in commentary, not in the verse)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a ladder of twelve stations, each paired with a letter, climbed and released one at a time through gross, subtle and supreme phases.
geometry.svg_hint: a vertical ladder of twelve rungs, each rung fading after it is passed
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Climb and release
reaction.summary: School metaphor: effort that moves piece by piece is released at each step until only continuity remains. Not a biochemical claim.

breath.lands_in: ordinary, even breath while attention climbs
breath.cue: Equal inhale four, exhale four if counting helps. Keep the breath quiet and even. No forced retention.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Orient upward one station at a time, leaving each one behind
orientation.gravity: Body supported; the climb is in attention only
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: One station at a time: feel it coarsely, then subtly, then let it go and rise
attention.secondary: The release itself, each time a station is left

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: Twelve stations in sequence, each properly marked by one of twelve letters: attend to each in its gross, then subtle, then supreme form, leaving each behind in turn; in the end there is Śiva.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method (Singh's notes): twelve stations from janmāgra to vyāpinī, linked with the twelve vowels, each contemplated in gross, subtle and supreme phases and then left behind. School simplification (flagged): move attention up a short midline sequence (pelvic floor, navel, heart, throat, brow, crown). At each station feel the coarse sense, then a subtler quiet, then leave it and rise. No phoneme placement, no forced breath-hold.

honesty.disclosure: Door 007 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 7 (verse 30) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 007 is dharana 7, verse 30. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.
School simplification: six midline stations are taught instead of the twelve stations and twelve vowels in Singh's notes.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. [retired posture] is paired with VBT dharana 007 by school index, not by historical one-to-one tradition.
legacy.notes: Mild experiential rhyme only: [retired posture] holds a continuous midline while dharana 007 moves attention station-to-station along central stations and leaves each. Classical verse 30 includes janmāgra (generative tip); School class form omits that station and starts at pelvic floor / navel. That rhyme and omission do not upgrade pairing beyond school_device.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. The school form is a simplification. It leaves out the vowel placements and the first commentarial station (janmāgra, at the level of the generative organ), and stops at the crown instead of continuing to the two stations beyond the body (śakti, vyāpinī). If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: Drop knees to the floor ([retired posture]), elevate hands on blocks or a chair, or take a short hold and rest in [retired posture]. Wrists may turn slightly outward or use fists/forearms if hands complain—keep the long line.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease out if wrists, shoulders, or low back turn sharp. Do not sag or pike through pain. Shorten the hold rather than collapse the line. Pregnancy and wrist concerns: prefer [retired posture], elevated hands, or skip the hold.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 007: twelve stations, twelve letters. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 7, verse 30.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Any easy seat, or lie down. The map is a ladder of stations up the centre of the body. We use a short six-step version.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body supported. Eyes closed or lowered. Orient upward, one station at a time.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Equal breath, four in, four out. No forced retention.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Pelvic floor, navel, heart, throat, brow, crown: feel each coarsely, then subtly, then leave it and rise.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: piece-by-piece effort is released into continuity. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 30: twelve stations, twelve letters, each held in gross, subtle and supreme form and then released; at the end, Śiva. Our form is simplified and safe: no drills on any genital station.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the ladder go. Rest one breath at the top in open space. Open the eyes.
